column1: # Redaction (ISO 32000-2:2020, 12.5.6.23). annotate: <path> index=N [kind=Redact x= y= width= height= | quads=8k numbers] [color=] [delete=K] [saved]: the page's
# annotations, ';'-joined, each 'Kind x,y,w,h[ q=quads][ c=colour without #]' in page coordinates, 4 fraction digits; 'none' when there are none.
# redact: <path> [marks=page@x,y,w,h[@rrggbb];...] [pages=list] [cancel[=N]] [mode=] read=...: adds the marks, applies them, saves, reopens and reads; a failed apply gives its
# code when the saves before and after give the same bytes and the marks stay, else '<code> changed'. cancel=N lets N progress calls through, and none reporting more done than
# its total. Coordinates are page coordinates; renders are at 72 per inch.
# A mark over a rectangle or quadrilaterals is listed, deleted and kept by a save (12.5.2, 12.5.6.23: Rect, QuadPoints, IC).
# A handle keeps to its annotation, written directly in Annots, after another is deleted; deleted, it is stale (12.5.2). delete=K,...: one listing's Kth, in turn.
# A mark needs a positive size or quadrilaterals of 8 finite numbers each, each with an area, and a valid colour.
# Every glyph whose box meets a mark is removed and found nowhere in the file; the rest of the page stays text (9.2.4, 9.4.3, 9.6.5).
# QuadPoints that cover no area give way to Rect (12.5.6.23).
# So do QuadPoints not of 8 numbers each; strict, they are malformed.
# Text in rendering mode 3, clipped away or in a hidden layer (9.3.6, 8.5.4, 8.11.3).
# Or at size 0, drawn nowhere: the text after it keeps its place (9.3.2, 9.4.4).
# An embedded Type 1 font shown by TJ with kerning partly under the mark: the glyphs after keep their place (9.4.3, 9.6.2).
# Type 3 glyphs: one partly under the mark, and ones that draw only outside their advance (9.6.4).
# A glyph procedure's stroke reaches as far as the line width where the glyph is shown (8.4.3.2, 9.6.4).
# Text that clips, all of it under the mark, leaves the clip empty (9.3.6).
# Text shown outside a text object, which no reader agrees where to draw (9.4.1).
# A show whose last operand is no string shows and moves nothing, BT within a text object begins none, and a TJ of no array leaves the text object open (9.4.1, 9.4.3).
# An operator that cannot be read, and an XObject neither image nor form, which no reader draws, go from a redacted page (7.8.2, 8.8).
# A stroked glyph reaches half the line width past its box (9.3.6).
# Miter joins reach half the line width times the miter limit (8.4.3.5, 9.3.6).
# A form XObject drawn under a mark and outside it, and a nested form under a mark (8.10).
# A thousand uses of a form, each cut under its own matrix; forms nested 13 deep, each drawing the next twice, whose same copies are one within a 1 MiB limit (8.10.1).
# What a mark removed leaves resources inherited from the page tree, shared with a page that does not use it, or shared with a form (7.7.3.4, 7.8.3).
# Or with a Type 3 glyph procedure or a soft mask group that another page draws through them (9.6.4, 11.6.5.2).
# Or a shading pattern's soft mask group (8.7.4.2, 11.6.5.2).
# Or with a kept annotation's appearance, through its own Resources or the page's (12.5.5).
# Or what only such an appearance, or a tiling pattern without Resources, names (7.8.3, 8.7.3.1).
# A hundred and fifty pages, each drawing a shared image under its mark by a name of its own: it goes.
# The content a redacted page no longer draws is gone, though named elsewhere, unless another page draws it (7.3.10, 14.5).
# An operator split between content streams is changed whole; the streams no mark changes stay (7.8.2).
# A touched optional content group or membership dictionary keeps its object, which visibility goes by: what is hidden stays hidden, here and on other pages (8.11.2, 8.11.4, 14.9.3).
# A change at the start of a content stream leaves the stream before it as it is (7.8.2).
# A touched property list in shared resources loses its words unless kept content elsewhere names it (14.6.2, 14.9.3 to 14.9.5).
# A name to what a mark removed goes from the resources of a page that never draws it (7.8.3).
# So does one a form on another page draws through resources of its own that the redacted page shared (7.8.3, 8.10.1).
# So does one only a graphics state or a form's own resources on another page name (7.3.10, 8.10.1, 11.6.5.2).
# A page whose Contents or Parent is damaged draws nothing; nor does a form its resources list that nothing draws (7.7.3.3, 7.7.3.4, 8.10.1).
# A button's icon and a template page draw what they name (7.7.4, 12.5.6.19).
# Or one drawn content uses as it is drawn, here the soft mask of an image outside the mark (7.3.10, 11.6.5.3).
# ActualText, Alt and E of marked content a mark touches, inline or named in Properties (14.6, 14.9.3, 14.9.4, 14.9.5).
# Of structure elements a mark touches through MCIDs or an OBJR, and of their ancestors (14.7.2, 14.7.4.4, 14.7.5).
# Of the element of a form that is one content item (14.7.5.3).
# Of the element of a pop-up removed with its parent (12.5.6.14, 14.7.5.4).
# Elements of a form or image a mark copies or removes refer to the copy, or no longer to it (14.7.4.3, 14.7.5.3).
# A parent tree leaf without its required Limits is still read (7.9.7).
# Images (8.9): one wholly under a mark is removed, an untouched one keeps its bytes. images= counts the Do of image XObjects, inline= the BI.
# Samples whose area meets a mark become 0 and transparent: a 1-bit Mask is added (1 masked, 8.9.6.3) or the SMask sample is 0 (11.6.5.3); samples are hex, row by row.
# Samples an image's data lacks stay unpainted (8.9.5).
# Inline images (8.9.7): one wholly under goes, one partly under becomes an image XObject.
# A stencil mask leaves covered samples unpainted (8.9.6.2), an explicit Mask masks them (8.9.6.3), a colour key gives them its value (8.9.6.4).
# A colour key no sample meets cannot hide samples replaced: a mask does (8.9.6.4).
# A soft mask finer than its image hides the whole of each sample replaced (11.6.5.3).
# A DCT image of two flat blocks, 64 and 192 (ITU-T T.81, A.3.3), partly covered, is re-encoded without loss.
# Paths (8.5.3): no coordinate strictly inside a mark remains, through cm and form matrices; shadings and patterns are clipped (8.7).
# A clip wholly inside a mark keeps nothing (8.5.4); a dash set by a graphics state dictionary is cut in phase (8.4.3.6, 8.4.5).
# Stroke ink that reaches a mark under a flipped, scaled matrix is clipped out of it (8.4.3.2); no control point of a curve stays in a mark (8.5.2.2).
# A move alone under a mark goes (8.5.2.1).
# A path of 16,502 points, fewer than the renderer draws, is cut (8.5.2).
# A graphics state whose soft mask cannot be read keeps its other parameters (8.4.5, 11.6.5.2).
# Under a singular matrix a fill or clip paints nothing, so nothing is removed (8.4.4).
# Overlapping marks are cut and clipped as their union: what lies between them stays (8.5.3, 8.5.4).
# Four hundred marks over an image and paths, each meeting few (8.9.5, 8.5.3).
# Four hundred marks over 6400 glyphs in 800 marked-content sequences, the page's parent tree key after a thousand others (9.4.3, 14.7.5.4).
# Annotations whose Rect meets a mark go with their popups, a widget with its field; a redacted page loses its thumbnail (12.3.4, 12.5.6.14, 12.7.4).
# Or whose appearance, NoRotate turning it upright about its top-left corner on a rotated page, does (12.5.3).
# A field removed with its widget leaves the calculation order (12.7.3.3).
# Two hundred widgets under the mark, each a field of the form, go within a 64 KiB limit (12.7.4).
# A kept annotation loses its IRT and Popup where they are removed (12.5.6.4, 12.5.6.14).
# So does one on another page (12.5.6.4).
# So do annotations and marks written in Annots (12.5.2).
# Only annotations go: a widget's Parent of another generation finds nothing, and a Popup naming the catalog leaves it (7.3.10, 12.5.2).
# Each mark's area is filled with its IC, or left empty without one, and the marks are gone (12.5.6.23).
# Marked content left open, here of a hidden layer, is closed before the fill (14.6, 8.11.3).
# Rendered before and after, pixels are the same outside the marks and except=: ink a mark removes whole, and within one line width of a cut stroke, whose coverage the renderer rounds anew.
# pages= limits the pages: none given is all, empty is none, one past the last is InvalidArgument.
# A page tree reaching more nodes and pages than the file has objects is malformed: they would be visited without end, here 2^30 nodes after a page (7.7.3.2).
# A root Count below the pages the tree holds still reaches every page, and progress never reports more done than its total (7.7.3.2).
# What cannot be removed fails and leaves the document unchanged: a font not embedded (9.6.2.2), an image of an unknown filter (7.4), text in a pattern cell (8.7.3); so does a cancel.
# So is one a cell paints with, a soft mask a cell sets, and one that paints text or a stencil mask under a mark (8.7.3.1, 8.9.6.2, 11.6.5.2).
# So is a soft mask group of a shading pattern that paints under a mark (8.7.4.2, 11.6.5.2).
# So is a Type 3 glyph under a mark whose procedure shows text or an image, which would stay in the font (9.6.4).
# An incremental save would keep the removed content in the old bytes (7.5.6).
